argument_summary: The admissible record does not support an unconditional certification, but it does support a constrained certification position. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.4 points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and deployment is limited to a 6% initial rollout with rollback and monitoring. The limiting fact is also clear: the field-service dispatch segment remains below target on technician safety-note routing, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that record, the defensible audit treatment is to read the certification request narrowly: certification is supportable only if the final certification package preserves explicit model-card disclosure of the field-service dispatch limitation rather than implying that rollout controls alone cure it.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated compliance treatment is lower cost than escalation because it preserves the existing launch path while keeping the limitation explicit in the record. The admissible evidence already supports bounded deployment and monitoring controls, so the remaining issue is scope and disclosure discipline, not a need to reopen the whole launch decision.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not allow rollout size, rollback capability, or monitoring to eliminate disclosure duties while the affected use case remains exposed. The policy threshold can still be met on this record if certification is treated as caveated compliance conditioned on explicit disclosure of the material limitation in the certification/model-card package. That interpretation narrows the claim to what the admissible evidence actually supports and avoids relying on the unsigned, non-covering risk-acceptance draft.
concessions: The field-service dispatch segment remains below target on technician safety-note routing and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case, so they do not by themselves satisfy the policy exception.
The current risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the field-service dispatch exposure.
Any unconditional reading of 'certify_model' would be broader than the admissible support.
